claim: Patchline computes a typed, minimal, reversible edit script between two schema snapshots so a reviewer sees exactly which columns are added, dropped, or altered, and can mechanically undo the change. The worker derives the canonical edit script from snapshot A to snapshot B, applies it to A to reproduce B, inverts it, applies the inverse to B to reproduce A, and checks minimality (no column touched twice, no alter whose before equals after). The gate proves the script is reversible in both directions and that a deliberately redundant script with a no-op alter and a duplicate touch is detected as non-minimal.
